depiction.subject: Museum panel with Dharmasokadeva copper coin dated 1208 CE and text on Polonnaruwa coinage
depiction.event_or_theme: monetary debasement and royal coinage in late Polonnaruwa
depiction.notes: The panel explicitly links Kahapana/Masu terminology to depreciation and describes copper/base-metal issues, silver wash and continued circulation of earlier gold and foreign coins.

vision_review.visual_notes: Two sides of the coin are shown above a trilingual museum text; English text is legible enough to preserve as field observation.
vision_review.uncertainty: The panel's causal interpretation of depreciation is a museum synthesis and must be independently tested.

tag_review.notes: Tagged to A04 monetary-stress thread; no stronger collapse causality inferred from image alone.

human_review.notes: User supplied the image and requested integration; reader-facing placement still follows project human-review gate.

fragment.caption: À la fin de Polonnaruwa, la monnaie royale raconte elle aussi un changement de régime matériel : le panneau montre un massa de cuivre de Dharmasokadeva (1208) et décrit la progression des émissions de métal vil.
fragment.what_it_shows: A museum synthesis of late-Polonnaruwa coinage with a 1208 copper issue.
fragment.why_here: Provides a concrete field object for the monetary-stress question and links numismatics to the wider collapse debate.
fragment.limits: The photograph documents the museum's synthesis; it does not by itself establish fiscal crisis, inflation or causal responsibility for the end of Polonnaruwa.
